newsitem.title: USA: Duramed, Barr shares fall again on FDA ruling.
newsitem.headline: Duramed, Barr shares fall again on FDA ruling.

text.p: Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc. and Barr Laboratories Inc. shares fell for a second day in a row Tuesday after the government rejected Duramed's application to market a synthetic generic form of Premarin, an oestrogen-replacement drug.
Barr has also applied to the Food and Drug Administration for clearance for a similar drug.
Cincinnati-based Duramed's stock plunged $5.75 to $4.625 on Nasdaq. Pomona, N.Y.-based Barr slid $2.25 to $41 on the American Stock Exchange.
"It's a severe blow for Duramed," said Ohio Co. industry analyst Eugene Robinson. "I don't know that a government agency has ever run a company into the ground like this before."
On Monday, the Food and Drug Administration said it will not approve synthetic generic forms of Premarin, which is produced as a brand-name drug by American Home Products Corp.
Duramed and Barr had filed market-clearance applications for a generic synthetic equivalent, the agency said.
The FDA said the generic version does not have the same active ingredients as American Home's brand name version, which is refined from horse urine.
Duramed and Barr could not be reached for comment.
